title: Make up a compression joint: pipe home, olive before nut, nut a turn past snug with a spanner
instruction: Join the copper pipe to the valve with the compression fitting.
context: Compression fittings join copper pipe to valves, taps and appliances in every building. Making one up has a standard: the pipe fully home into the fitting's socket, the olive on before the nut so that it sits between the nut and the fitting, and the nut turned about a turn past snug (3/4 to 1 1/4). A forgotten or misplaced olive, or a pipe short of its stop, leaks; much further, the olive and the pipe are crushed. Done by: plumbers, pipefitters and steamfitters (O*NET 47-2152.00), heating and air-conditioning mechanics (49-9021.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); the layout is the same in every trial. Fixed: a 15 mm brass compression ball valve on a wooden mounting block (6 x 4 cm) at x 30, y -3, its inlet facing up (the thread stub's top 4.2 cm up, the socket's stop 3 cm up), a red paint line on its body's top and side (+x) at the snug angle. Loose: a 15 mm copper pipe tail (6 cm, pencil-marked 12 mm from its end) standing in a drilled wooden block (4.4 x 4.4 x 2.5 cm) at x 20, y 17; a brass olive (17.5 mm across, 7 mm long) and the brass compression nut (22 mm across flats, 12 mm tall, a red paint mark on a flat and its top face), lying on a wooden tray (6 x 11 x 1 cm) at x 27, y 6 and y 11; a 22 mm open-ended chrome spanner (0.1 kg, 13 cm) lying on its board at x 22, y -17, its jaw at x 27, the handle pointing to -x.
scoring: Measured from the video and at the end, with the pencil mark on the pipe and the snug marks: the nut's red mark lines up with the red line on the valve body when the nut is snug on a new olive (the line is set before the trials with a torque wrench at 2 N m on three new olives of the batch; see the README), so turns past snug are the turns of the nut's mark past the line, counted on the video. 0 if at any point the nut was turned more than 1 1/4 turns past snug (olive over-compressed; more than 1 1/2: crushed). Otherwise: 1.0 if sealed (pipe home, its end within 1 mm of the stop; the olive under the nut; the nut 3/4 to 1 1/4 turns past snug), the spanner back in its tray, no part of either gripper within 1 cm of the spanner, nut or pipe, the spanner and pipe still (under 1 cm/s) for 1 s; 0.5 if sealed but not as for 1.0; 0.25 if the pipe is home and the olive under the nut on the thread, the nut under 3/4 turn past snug; else 0 (no olive, olive outside the nut, pipe short).
reset_notes: Undo the nut, lift the pipe out, cut the olive off and fit a new one (olives are not reused once compressed); stand the pipe in its holder and put the nut, olive and spanner in their trays.
fidelity: PhysX cannot cut a thread or compress an olive: our model. The socket holds the pipe on the axis; rings dropped over its top are kept centred and slide down; the olive rests in the stub's cone, the nut on it. Resting there the nut is on the thread and posed: 1.8 mm a turn, snug after 1 turn (real run-on 3-4), crushed 1.5 turns past. A spanner jaw on the flats within 3 mm turns it; the jaws are drawn only (the model holds them on the nut). No torque. Boxes, real sizes.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the left hand reaches down over the parts tray and the right over the spanner's board, but nothing is picked up or assembled); demo: 1.0 (success at step 1,913)
